judge: claude-opus-5-5 via claude -p (l7a subscription), image + OCR + English + previous page tail, blind to arm

high_findings.name: P02
high_findings.title: 尚書纂傳·卷十四上~卷十六 (vol 4)
high_findings.source_span: 劉殺也
high_findings.english_span: "Value" means sparing
high_findings.why: The gloss says 劉 (liu) means 'to kill'. The English attaches it to the wrong word and reverses its meaning to 'sparing'.

high_findings.name: P21
high_findings.title: 欽定春秋傳說彙纂·卷五 (vol 29)
high_findings.source_span: 大子無敵
high_findings.english_span: The Crown Prince <note>or sovereign</note> has no equal
high_findings.why: The context makes this the Son of Heaven (天子, here written 大子). 'Crown Prince' brings in a different person, and the note only half fixes it.

high_findings.name: P30
high_findings.title: 黃氏日抄·卷三十二 (vol 24)
high_findings.source_span: 二十七 顏子驕瑯琊伯
high_findings.english_span:
Qidiao Lian, Count of Wucheng, 26.

Qidiao Tufu, Count of Xuju, 27.
high_findings.why: The entry for Yan Zijiao, Count of Langya, is missing, so the reader gets one disciple fewer.

high_findings.name: P30
high_findings.title: 黃氏日抄·卷三十二 (vol 24)
high_findings.source_span: 二十八 壤駟赤…三十四 (next page)
high_findings.english_span: Qidiao Tufu, Count of Xuju, 27. … Gongliang Ru, Count of Dongmou, 33.
high_findings.why: The number follows each entry, so these seven should be 28–34 (Qidiao Tufu 28 … Gongliang Ru 34; 三十四 opens the next page), but the dropped entry shifts each one down by one.

high_findings.name: P37
high_findings.title: 後漢書[范煜…等撰]·卷九十三~卷九十五 (Hou Hanshu, Siku Quanshu, vol. 33 of 43)
high_findings.source_span: 得其人與不在盧生耳
high_findings.english_span: Have suitable men been obtained? Let us not rely solely on master Lu.
high_findings.why: The edict says that whether the right men are found depends on Master Lu (Lu Yu) alone. The English reverses this and tells people not to rely on him.

high_findings.name: P39
high_findings.title: 記纂淵海·卷三十八~卷三十九 (vol 24)
high_findings.source_span: 親有嚴客希
high_findings.english_span: When one's parents entertain an honored guest, rarely
high_findings.why: The image shows 帣 ('to roll up the sleeves'), not 希. The English 'rarely' breaks the sentence (Shiji: 帣韝鞠䐐，侍酒於前).

high_findings.name: P41
high_findings.title: 前漢書·卷五十五~卷五十六 (Hanshu, Siku Quanshu, vol. 33 of 57)
high_findings.source_span: 臣召南
high_findings.english_span: <gloss>Quan Zhaonan, 1710–1768, Qing dynasty historian</gloss>
high_findings.why: The Siku Hanshu kaozheng author 召南 is Qi Zhaonan 齊召南 (1703–1768). The gloss gives a surname and dates that are not in the source, and both are wrong.

high_findings.name: P01
high_findings.title: 圖書編·卷一百二十七 (vol 97)
high_findings.source_span: 瓊瑰 瓊瑰玉佩 (OCR 瓊瓊 / 璁 璁璁)
high_findings.english_span: Excellent fine jade / Green-colored jade / Brilliant green jade
high_findings.why: The image reads 瓊瑰 / 瓊瑰玉佩 ('fine jade stones and jade pendants'). The OCR's 璁 led to a made-up 'green jade' entry.

high_findings.name: P01
high_findings.title: 圖書編·卷一百二十七 (vol 97)
high_findings.source_span: 觿 童子佩觿 (OCR 簫 / 佩鱬)
high_findings.english_span: The jade fish-shaped pendant
high_findings.why: The image reads 佩觿 (a knot-untying spike). The OCR's 鱬 produced an invented fish pendant.

high_findings.name: P01
high_findings.title: 圖書編·卷一百二十七 (vol 97)
high_findings.source_span: 瑳兮 (OCR 珽 兮)
high_findings.english_span: The jade tablet <note>original: "珽"</note>
high_findings.why: The image reads 瑳兮瑳兮. No jade-tablet entry exists on the page.

high_findings.name: P03
high_findings.title: 御定康熙字典·卷十八 (vol 53)
high_findings.source_span: 猶 (headword; image shows 犭+隋), 集韻選委切音髓
high_findings.english_span: ### Yǔ
high_findings.why: The headword is 犭+隋, read suǐ (音髓); the OCR has 猶 and the English heading gives 'Yǔ', a reading that fits neither character.

high_findings.name: P03
high_findings.title: 御定康熙字典·卷十八 (vol 53)
high_findings.source_span: 或作獺…一作獺…本作獺 (image: 犭+隋-type variant forms)
high_findings.english_span: <term>tǎ</term> <gloss>otter-like animal</gloss>
high_findings.why: The variant forms are 犭+隋-type graphs, not 獺; 'otter' is a gloss the source never gives.

high_findings.name: P03
high_findings.title: 御定康熙字典·卷十八 (vol 53)
high_findings.source_span: 獼 (headword; image 犭+麻), 狼狄切音歷
high_findings.english_span: ### Mí
high_findings.why: The headword is 犭+麻, read lì; the heading 'Mí' comes from the OCR's 獼.

high_findings.name: P03
high_findings.title: 御定康熙字典·卷十八 (vol 53)
high_findings.source_span: 獫 (headword; image 犭+壹), 虛器切音齂
high_findings.english_span: ### Xiǎn … sounding like <term>fú</term>
high_findings.why: The headword is 犭+壹 (xì), not 獫, and the homophone is 齂, not 韍 (fú).

high_findings.name: P03
high_findings.title: 御定康熙字典·卷十八 (vol 53)
high_findings.source_span: 夏后氏有獟獞寒浞子名
high_findings.english_span: the Xia Dynasty official Han Zhuo had sons named <term>Yáo</term> and <term>Tóng</term>
high_findings.why: The source names one person in the Xia era, Han Zhuo's son (the headword); it does not make Han Zhuo a Xia official or give him two sons.

high_findings.name: P03
high_findings.title: 御定康熙字典·卷十八 (vol 53)
high_findings.source_span: 獙 (headword; image 犭+敢), 荒檻切
high_findings.english_span: ### Bì
high_findings.why: The headword is 犭+敢, read hǎn (the English body itself says so); the heading 'Bì' comes from the OCR's 獙.

high_findings.name: P06
high_findings.title: 御定子史精華·卷一百二十三~卷一百二十四 (vol 143)
high_findings.source_span: 不能曰不能行之至也
high_findings.english_span: To say that one "cannot" is the peak of being unable to act.
high_findings.why: This finishes the previous page's 能之曰能之: 'when unable, he says he is unable; that is the height of conduct'. The English turns it into a statement about the peak of inability.

high_findings.name: P06
high_findings.title: 御定子史精華·卷一百二十三~卷一百二十四 (vol 143)
high_findings.source_span: 戰者不習使人戰者嚴駔
high_findings.english_span: If those who do not practice are made to fight, it is because their leaders are severe and forceful.
high_findings.why: Here 戰 means 'tremble': 'trembling comes from being unaccustomed; one who makes others tremble is harsh'. It is not about combat, so the 'On Combat' heading is also wrong.

high_findings.name: P06
high_findings.title: 御定子史精華·卷一百二十三~卷一百二十四 (vol 143)
high_findings.source_span: 申向說之而戰…申子說我而戰為吾相也夫
high_findings.english_span: Shen Xiang spoke to him and incited a desire for war. Lord Ta criticized him, saying, "Master Shen, you speak to me of war because I am the Chancellor."
high_findings.why: Shen Xiang trembled while speaking to him. He was not urging war.

high_findings.name: P06
high_findings.title: 御定子史精華·卷一百二十三~卷一百二十四 (vol 143)
high_findings.source_span: 見老者而使之戰
high_findings.english_span: When you see an elder, you make him go to war.
high_findings.why: The meaning is that the lord receives an old man and makes him tremble. There is no going to war.

high_findings.name: P10
high_findings.title: 御定佩文韻府·卷一百二之八 (vol 719)
high_findings.source_span: 生輝光
high_findings.english_span: Produces brilliance.
high_findings.why: 生輝光 ends the Bai Juyi line from the previous page (拂拭生輝光). The English turns it into a new headword.

high_findings.name: P10
high_findings.title: 御定佩文韻府·卷一百二之八 (vol 719)
high_findings.source_span: 丨丨 (=拂拭) throughout first entry
high_findings.english_span: <term>shanghui</term> <gloss>producing brilliance</gloss>
high_findings.why: In every quotation 丨丨 stands for the headword 拂拭 'to dust/wipe', not the invented 'shanghui', so all eleven quotations are mistranslated.

high_findings.name: P10
high_findings.title: 御定佩文韻府·卷一百二之八 (vol 719)
high_findings.source_span: 丨丨魚鱗見
high_findings.english_span: Under the shanghui the fish scales appear
high_findings.why: It means 'when wiped, fish-scale patterns appear'.

high_findings.name: P10
high_findings.title: 御定佩文韻府·卷一百二之八 (vol 719)
high_findings.source_span: 丨丨輕塵宛是昔年之字
high_findings.english_span: the shanghui producing brilliance light dust is exactly as the characters
high_findings.why: It means 'wiping off the light dust, the characters are just as in former years'.

high_findings.name: P10
high_findings.title: 御定佩文韻府·卷一百二之八 (vol 719)
high_findings.source_span: 馬能為繞指丨丨試時人
high_findings.english_span: A horse can wind around the finger
high_findings.why: The character is 焉 'how could', not 馬 'horse': 'how could it become finger-soft? Wipe it and test it on the men of the day'.

high_findings.name: P10
high_findings.title: 御定佩文韻府·卷一百二之八 (vol 719)
high_findings.source_span: 朱博傳
high_findings.english_span: Biography of Zhu Boru
high_findings.why: The man is Zhu Bo (朱博). 'Boru' is invented.

high_findings.name: P10
high_findings.title: 御定佩文韻府·卷一百二之八 (vol 719)
high_findings.source_span: 府功曹白除禁守尉
high_findings.english_span: reported this and removed Jin from his post as a guard
high_findings.why: 除 here means 'appoint': the officer recommended appointing Jin as acting commandant, not removing him.

high_findings.name: P10
high_findings.title: 御定佩文韻府·卷一百二之八 (vol 719)
high_findings.source_span: 欲瀧卿恥丨丨用禁能自效不
high_findings.english_span: If you can prove yourself, I will not forbid it.
high_findings.why: It means 'I want to wash away your shame and wipe the slate clean by employing you, Jin; can you exert yourself?' 不禁 is misparsed as 'will not forbid'. 瀧 is a misread of 灑 'wash away'.

high_findings.name: P17
high_findings.title: 御定子史精華·卷八十四~卷八十六 (vol 129)
high_findings.source_span: 長事袁絲弟畜灌夫籍福之屬
high_findings.english_span: served him. Yuan Si treated him like a younger brother, and people like Guan Fu and Ji Fu were associated with him
high_findings.why: Ji Xin served Yuan Si as an elder brother and treated Guan Fu and Ji Fu as younger brothers. The English reverses who treated whom as a younger brother.

high_findings.name: P17
high_findings.title: 御定子史精華·卷八十四~卷八十六 (vol 129)
high_findings.source_span: 坐其兄蓋侯南鄉自坐東鄉
high_findings.english_span: an act of humility or subordinate positioning
high_findings.why: Facing east was the seat of honour. Tian Fen was claiming precedence over his elder brother, so this note says the opposite of what happened.

high_findings.name: P18
high_findings.title: 武經總要前集·卷六~卷七 (vol 3)
high_findings.source_span: 欠已曰事已
high_findings.english_span: <unclear>Words missing or illegible</unclear> said: "The matter is finished."
high_findings.why: The OCR misread the margin running head (欽定四庫全書) as text. The English turns it into a made-up quotation from an unnamed speaker that is not on the page.

high_findings.name: P23
high_findings.title: 御定佩文韻府·卷一百二之七 (vol 718)
high_findings.source_span: 懷慝 魏志武帝紀吏無苛政民無懷慝
high_findings.english_span: **Vicious Evil** <note>original: 凶慝</note> The Records of Wei... the people shall have no vicious evil
high_findings.why: This quote belongs under the 懷慝 headword and reads 'harbor no evil'. The English files it under 凶慝 and renders it 'vicious evil'.

high_findings.name: P23
high_findings.title: 御定佩文韻府·卷一百二之七 (vol 718)
high_findings.source_span: 陰搆凶慝大將軍糾度天刑
high_findings.english_span: The military investigated and carried out the heavenly punishment
high_findings.why: The OCR dropped 大將 from 大將軍, so the subject 'the Grand General' became 'the military', which changes who acted.

high_findings.name: P23
high_findings.title: 御定佩文韻府·卷一百二之七 (vol 718)
high_findings.source_span: 三垂剪除凶慝好惡同之
high_findings.english_span: eliminate those who harbor emotional evil
high_findings.why: The repeat marks here stand for 凶慝, because the Tang shu quote sits under that headword and comes before the 情慝 heading. The English moves it under 'Emotional Evil'.

high_findings.name: P31
high_findings.title: 御定子史精華·卷六十三~卷六十四 (vol 70)
high_findings.source_span: 丨丨丨丨丨丨餳酒賦詩
high_findings.english_span: <note>from the context of the Sui Shu</note>
high_findings.why: The note cites the Sui Shu, but this passage comes from Song-history material; nothing in the source supports the note.

high_findings.name: P31
high_findings.title: 御定子史精華·卷六十三~卷六十四 (vol 70)
high_findings.source_span: 由選人至兩地財四年
high_findings.english_span: <note>referring to Li Mi</note>
high_findings.why: Li Mi is not named in the source. This phrase is the heading for Chen Ziqiang's entry, but the note assigns it to an invented person.

high_findings.name: P31
high_findings.title: 御定子史精華·卷六十三~卷六十四 (vol 70)
high_findings.source_span: 故事比攝官丨丨丨丨(奉饋如真)
high_findings.english_span: Gifts and offerings were presented to him as if to a god.
high_findings.why: 奉饋如真 is the heading for Wu Changyi's entry. It means acting officials drew the same stipend as substantive officials. It is not about gifts given to Chen Ziqiang as a god.

high_findings.name: P31
high_findings.title: 御定子史精華·卷六十三~卷六十四 (vol 70)
high_findings.source_span: 婁機傳調含山主簿丨丨丨丨(七攝鄰邑)率以治績聞
high_findings.english_span: He served as an acting official for neighboring districts seven times.
high_findings.why: 七攝鄰邑 is the heading for Lou Ji's entry and fills the 丨 marks in his text. The English credits it to Wu Changyi, which changes who did it.

high_findings.name: P45
high_findings.title: 御定子史精華·卷六十五~卷六十七 (vol 71)
high_findings.source_span: 因丨丨丨丨而丨丨丨丨
high_findings.english_span: Because he Zheng Qi Ci Ju refined the phrasing and Shen Qi Tan Lun scrutinized the discussions
high_findings.why: The marks repeat the headword 斟酌前史/譏正得失. The terms Zheng Qi Ci Ju and Shen Qi Tan Lun and their glosses appear nowhere in the source.

high_findings.name: P45
high_findings.title: 御定子史精華·卷六十五~卷六十七 (vol 71)
high_findings.source_span: 辨而不華 質而不野
high_findings.english_span: his work was: Elegant but not flowery. Plain but not crude.
high_findings.why: This is the headword for the next entry, Ban Biao's praise of Sima Qian (善述序事理，辨而不華…, which continues on the next page). The English makes it a description of Ban Biao's own work.

high_findings.name: P47
high_findings.title: 御定佩文韻府·卷八十之二 (vol 596)
high_findings.source_span: 茔
high_findings.english_span: *Ying* <gloss>grave mound</gloss>
high_findings.why: The image shows 莝 (cuo, chopped straw), which belongs to the 箇 rhyme. The OCR read it as 茔 (ying, grave), and the English gives a wrong headword and gloss.

high_findings.name: P47
high_findings.title: 御定佩文韻府·卷八十之二 (vol 596)
high_findings.source_span: 礎
high_findings.english_span: *Chu* <gloss>stone plinth</gloss>
high_findings.why: The image shows 磋 (cuo, to polish), a 箇-rhyme word. The OCR read it as 礎 (chu, plinth), which is not in this rhyme group.

high_findings.name: P08
high_findings.title: 圖書編·卷二十四 (vol 22)
high_findings.source_span: 一年始於建寅之月／為正子丑二月雖屬次年
high_findings.english_span: The months of Zi and Chou are regarded as correct for this purpose.
high_findings.why: 為正 finishes the previous page's sentence: the Yin month is taken as the first month (正). The English makes Zi and Chou the 'correct' months, which reverses the point.
